candidates.buyer: Independent hotels, guest houses, beach/entertainment operators, travel agencies and car rental firms in Monrovia and coastal counties
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
candidates.evidence: https://allafrica.com/stories/202603230708.html ; https://www.liberianobserver.com/news/register-or-shut-down/article_082a227d-8169-49f8-aaa0-fa28c6e50aa2.html ; https://atta.travel/resource/liberia-launches-nationwide-campaign-to-formalise-tourism-sector.html . WebFetch of the first two found no fees, documents, levy or deadline date, only the 90-day grace period and the closure threat.
candidates.existing: Competitor search (hotel software, guest house booking, PMS, LNTA levy, Monrovia) found no local vendor and no LNTA compliance tool; global PMS and booking platforms exist but none tied to the LNTA register.
candidates.name: LNTA tourism-business registration and inspection-readiness pack for hotels, guest houses and travel/car-rental firms
candidates.trigger: Liberia National Tourism Act 2025; LNTA nationwide campaign from March 2026 with a 90-day registration grace period then inspections, sanctions and possible closure; exact deadline and whether it was extended unconfirmed
candidates.unchecked: LNTA forms, fees, renewal cycle, guest-register or tourism-levy rule; whether the grace period was extended; size of the register; whether LNTA has an online portal.

candidates.unchecked: Competitor search not run; LACRA's required reports and registers for agents and warehouses; number of agents; overlap with K01 (EUDR) buyers.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: LPRC holds statutory import/storage control under the 1989 Acts; ~9 registered importers (West Oil, Total, Monrovia Oil Trading etc., undated). Senate passed a bill in March 2026 to reform LPRC and repeal the 1989 exclusive rights (enactment unconfirmed). No retail station licence procedure, register or recurring filing found; EPA permit angle noted under 32. Nothing concrete for a candidate; unverified.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: LACRA (Act 2014) licenses cocoa/coffee exporters and regulates buying agents; 2026 deployment of 47 inspectors to warehouses/collection points. Old reported thresholds: US$25k bank balance, US$10k fee (unverified current). Near K01 but different buyer (local buying agents/warehouses). Candidate L3.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: CDA is regulator with annual audit mandate (only 29 co-ops audited 2014-16, so mandate under-delivered); apex bodies LNFCS and LCUNA; VSLA/CSLA groups are NGO-run (200+ groups under Grassroot VSLA Apex). No mandatory recurring filing found beyond audit; low willingness to pay. Weak candidate L9.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: National Health Insurance bill (HEAL authority with accreditation and claims) delivered to the President on 22 June 2026, not yet operating; a digital health insurance pilot for vulnerable groups started July 2025. LMDC closed three private facilities in June 2026 over expired drugs and waste. Claims software premature; compliance side folded into L4. Unverified.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: LMHRA licenses premises, personnel and importers (2025 G2 Pharmacy import-licence suspension over labelling); Liberia Pharmacy Board closes unlicensed drug stores (e.g. Foya, Apr 2025) and requires Ministry of Finance business registration first. No renewal calendar or portal found. Candidate L4.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security licensed by MoJ Public Safety Department; no dedicated private security law confirmed (draft discussed); industry association calls for a compliance audit. Tenders demand tax clearance, business registration and MoJ certificate. Candidate L6 (weak). Cleaning and manpower agencies: nothing found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: MME licence classes: Class C (Liberians only, 25-acre placer claim, US$250 fee in 2016 schedule), rock quarry US$25k-50k, river sand US$25k-50k, laterite permits; Inspector-General verifying Class B/C licences; draft Minerals and Mining Law Jan 2024 (status unconfirmed). Candidate L2. Construction contractors and local-content reports not searched.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: AML/CFT/Proceeds of Crime Act 2021 and FIA Act 2021; FIA threatened fines for non-compliant DNFBPs (2021); new CDD directive and real-estate risk assessment in 2025-26 ahead of a third mutual evaluation. Which professions must report and thresholds were not confirmed. Candidate L5 (unverified).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Liberia National Tourism Act 2025 made LNTA a standalone regulator; March 2026 campaign gave hotels, travel agencies, entertainment centres and car rental firms a 90-day registration grace period, with inspections and possible closure after. No fees, forms, levy or guest-register rule found. Candidate L1.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Fish: NaFAA licences (2020 regulations), artisanal canoe fee cut to US$30 from 1 Jan 2026; EU IUU/traceability for exports. Timber: FDA chainsaw milling permits (Reg 115-11) only in community/private forest, chainsaw timber outside the LiberTrace system; relates to K05. Cocoa/coffee: LACRA, see 22 and K01. Candidates L7, L8.

coverage.category: 31. Artisanal mining, quarry and sand-mining licence holders
coverage.found: Country-specific category from the MME fee schedule (2016) and 2023-24 inspection drives; see 27 and candidate L2.

coverage.category: 32. EPA environmental permits for businesses and projects
coverage.found: EPA 2026 nationwide compliance drive: fines, monitoring fees and restoration costs; shutdown of a miner for an unrenewed permit (May 2026). Permit classes and renewal cycle for small businesses not found. Folded into L2.

Tax Amendment Act approved 24 Mar 2026, published 1 Apr 2026; GST to VAT in 2027 (LRA says 15%; a third-party guide says registration from 1 Jul 2026 and a rate near 18%, conflicting). LRA e-filing covers turnover tax, GST and withholding. Generic accounting territory, so out of scope as a product; weak candidate L10.

Employer registration and monthly contributions under NASSCORP General Regulations 2023; rates and deadlines conflict across sources (6% employer / 4% employee in one). Generic payroll, out of scope; weak candidate L11.

coverage.category: 36. Forestry chainsaw milling and lumber dealers (FDA)
37. Mobile money agents and telecom regulation (CBL / LTA)
coverage.found: Mobile Money Regulations CBL/RSD/003/2014 put agent due diligence and agent lists on providers (Lonestar MTN, Orange; Vita Money licensed by LTA); a 2025 Banking Act may have updated the framework. Duty falls mainly on providers, so adjacent to K04. Weak candidate L12.

coverage.category: 38. Business registration and beneficial-ownership declarations (LBR / LISCR)
coverage.found: 2020 Associations Law amendments require annual declarations of shareholders, beneficial owners and officers via registered agent (31 Dec cycle) for non-resident entities; domestic small-firm annual returns and penalties not found. Unverified, low priority.
